title: ingest fallback hypotheses and repro notes
content:
High-level summary:
- Night of 2026-02-19 ~22:10 UTC we saw a sudden drop in traced spans ingested by prod collector.
- Symptoms: traces/stats show span_ingest_rate drop from ~1200/s -> ~60/s for ~7 minutes, then intermittent bursts.
- Logs: collector instances returned repeated '504 upstream timeout' and 'failed to publish span: EOF' from kafka producer layer.

Why I think this matters:
- Affected services rely on sampling+prefix caching for downstream routing. Loss of spans causes missing traces in flame graphs and alerts firing (trace-based SLOs).
- We saw coincident CPU spikes on collector pods and a surge in consumer lag for the trace-topic.

What I did (commands + outputs):
- kubectl: check pods + restart one replica (no change):
  kubectl get pods -n infra | grep collector
  collector-5f8d7   2/2   Running   1   3d

- checked consumer lag (kafka-manager + kafkacat):
  kafkacat -C -b kafka-prod-broker:9092 -t traces-prod -o end -e
  # returned last offset check OK; but consumer group lag: 0 -> 40k during window

- polled logs for error snippets: (copied raw lines)
  2026-02-19T22:11:03Z ERROR producer.go:142 failed to publish span: EOF
  2026-02-19T22:11:03Z WARN otlp_exporter.go:78 tls handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
  2026-02-19T22:12:40Z ERROR batching.go:61 timeout sending batch: context deadline exceeded

- otel-collector probe (from debug pod):
  -> curl -v https://collector-internal.prod:4317/v1/traces
  * Connected to collector-internal.prod (10.5.2.13) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
  POST /v1/traces HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  < Retry-After: 5

- stack traces attached to collector pod around crash window: repeated goroutine dumps showing goroutines blocked on net/http.Client.Do

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Kafka broker leader bounce + producer backpressure -> producer errors + batching timeouts. Evidence: consumer group lag spike, producer EOFs, CPU rise. If true, we'd also see controller log lines on brokers.
2) TLS cert rotation partially deployed -> some collectors fail TLS handshake to internal collector endpoints (see tls: bad certificate). Could be mismatched certs between collectors and downstream TLS termination. This would cause 503s and 'bad certificate' warnings.
3) Rate-limiter config bug in collector: new config (deployed 2026-02-18) added aggressive max inflight/batch size causing backpressure under burst traffic. Evidence: new release PR https://github.com/redwood/collector/pull/412 and config flip in INFRA-234.
4) Autoscaler churn: HPA scaled pods down while kube-proxy rebalanced connections leading to transient errors. Less likely because restart count low.

Commands to reproduce locally (rough):
- Start local collector with prod config:
  make dev-collector && \OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://collector-internal.staging:4317 \OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service=test curl -X POST --data-binary @sample-trace.pb https://localhost:4317/v1/traces -v
- Simulate broker failure: spin up local kafka, drop leader via kafka-topics --alter command to move partitions.

Quick checks to run next (short):
- grep broker logs for controller events around 22:10-22:20 (INFRA team) -> JIRA INFRA-234 assigned.
- validate cert chain: openssl s_client -connect collector-internal.prod:4317 -showcerts and compare fingerprint to secrets/certs/collector-cert-2026-02-17
- inspect recent rollout (kubectl rollout history) for collector deployment and exact image tag (was there a config-only rollout?)
- query metrics from prometheus: rate(collector_producer_errors_total[5m]) and partition_rebalance events; graph span_ingest_rate per region

Observed weirdness / inconsistent bits: 
- Some collector pods returned 200 for healthcheck while returning 503 on OTLP path (maybe readiness vs app-level error).
- Not all clusters affected (us-east impacted, eu-west fine) -> suggests network or broker partition per region rather than global config bug.

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Scaled collectors to +3 replicas in us-east to offload (manual). Not ideal; I reverted after 45m when traffic normalized.

Longer-term fixes to investigate: 
- Rollback PR #412 (if config change implicated) and re-run canary with traffic shaping.
- Add a canary script that sends synthetic traces through the OTLP path and asserts on both TLS handshake and producer success.
- Improve alerting: trigger on producer EOF and batching timeouts (currently only consumer lag alerts exist).

Open questions / unknowns I want help on: 
- Do we have broker controller logs preserved for 2026-02-19 window? Who owns retention? (cc INFRA)
- Were any certs rotated around 2026-02-18-19? (cc security)
- Is PR 412 definitely in prod or only in staging at the time? (cc release)

Next steps (concrete):
- [ ] Ask INFRA to confirm broker leader moves and share controller logs (INC-7842)
- [ ] Validate TLS cert fingerprints for collector endpoints (SRE)
- [ ] Run a rollback of config if we can reproduce locally quickly (owner: me)
- [ ] Add a short e2e synthetic trace check into deployment pipeline (owner: Priya)

Scratch/test notes (commands I ran yesterday, keep for repro):
- kubectl -n infra logs collector-5f8d7 -c collector --since=30m | grep EOF | head -n 20
- kubectl -n infra exec -it debug-pod -- openssl s_client -connect collector-internal.prod:4317 -servername collector-internal.prod < /dev/null | sed -n '1,120p'
- kafkacat -b kafka-prod-broker:9092 -t traces-prod -p 0 -C -o -100

Rough timeline (timestamps in UTC):
- 22:09: alert firing: span_ingest_rate drop detected
- 22:10: consumer lag rising; collector logs show EOF and tls errors
- 22:17: mitigation scaling +3 replicas
- 22:58: traffic normalizes, scale reverted

Notes to self: keep this file as ephemeral scratch — move any final findings to confluence page: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Ingest+Incidents

If you pick this up: start with cert check and INFRA controller logs. If both clean, pivot to reproducing producer backpressure locally with PR 412 config toggled.

-- Sofia
